messages.subject: spatio-temporal n-mix
parts:
I have bird abundance estimates over a thirty year period distributed throughout parts of the UK. It is highly likely that these abundance estimates have detectability issues.

My objective is to account for this detection and estimate abundance each year spatially throughout the country i.e. an abundance estimate for every site in every year

Ideally (based on my reading), I would like something similar to the 'pcountopen' approach, but with a spatial covariance matrix embedded, whereby abundances, and abundance trends, are spatially correlated. However, I realise this is probably unrealistic atm, but I am wondering, is there a way to embed nested random effects (region, county) as a proxy of this spatial structure within unmarked, whereby mean abundances (intercepts) and trends (slopes) can capture this process.

This spatial representation of the data is important as I need to predict abundance spatio-temporally.

I imagine this is possible in STAN, which I can code in, but I fear it will be far too slow for a dataset of my size

Best wishes, Tom

Dr Thomas F. Johnson
University of Sheffield

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] spatio-temporal n-mix
parts:
Dear Tom,

there is some support now for adding random effects into models fit in unmarked, using the TMB software as an engine under the hood. However, I don't think this is possible yet for the unmarked function that fits the Dail-Madsen model. Ken Kellner will know better.

Also, some limited forms of Nmix models can be fit with INLA (observational covariates are not possible, only site covariates), see here: https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v095i02


Best regards  --- Marc
